In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of human minor histocompatibility Ag-specific T cells.

the identification of novel minor H Ags that may be used as therapeutic targets in the context of allogeneic transplantation and the characterization of regulatory T cells that may be used to control the alloresponse.

the identification of novel minor histocompatibility Ags and of the T cell repertoire that recognizes them, with the aim to develop novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of graft-versus-host diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CD4/CD+ double-positive, minor H Ag-specific, graft-versus-host protective, regulatory T cells and the HLA-DR/7 HY-specific T cells are novel T cell populations that have not been previously described and are of potential interest for the treatment of acute graft-versus- host disease and for the prevention of graft rejection.

we have shown human CD4/ CD8 double-positive, graft-versus-host–protective, autosomal minor H Ag– specific regulatory T cells, and we have identified a new HLA-DR 7/HY T cell epitope encoded by RPS 4Y.

the three T cell populations described in this study are: 1) a novel CD4/CD 8 double-positive, HLA class I restricted, minor H Ag-specific regulatory T cell population, 2) an HLA class II restricted HY-specific cytotoxic T cell population and 3) an HLA- DR7/ HY-specific proliferative T cell population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel HLA class II-restricted HY epitope, encoded in RPS4Y.

we have isolated three different types of T cells from a single patient: 1) a CD4+/CD-8+ double-positive T cell that is specific for an H-Y Ag encoded by a gene located on chromosome 20; 2) an H-Y-specific CD8+ T cell that is weakly cytotoxic; and 3) a CD4+ single-positive T cell that recognizes a novel HLA class II–restricted HY epitopes, TGKIINIFIKFDTGN
the human immune response to a male-specific Ag is complex and includes both CD4 and CD8 T cell populations with regulatory and cytotoxic functions, which can be used to treat male-specific diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human CD4/ CD8 double-positive T cell subset is a novel source of graft-versus-host-disease–protective, regulatory, minor H Ag-specific T cells.
CD4/CD5 double-positive T cells are present and functional in humans and that they can be isolated in the presence of a strong inflammatory response.

CD4/CD 8 double positive cells can have regulatory function and that they are able to recognize minor H Ags, and therefore, may play a protective role in the context of acute graft-versus host disease.
